items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He saw me with Lionel Hampton and told Maynard that he should try to get me in the band. Maynard did.

ctx.x: I can’t say that I have, no.

Louis Jordan big band was very good, because Louis Jordan had enough money to pay – get great musicians, because from his little group he was very successful. In fact, he had to take the big band, because he was making so much money. So this guy was in the band. Then from that band, he went to Maynard’s band. He saw me with Lionel Hampton and told Maynard that he should try to get me in the band. Maynard did. Maynard was a very nice guy, a really great musician, and gave us the opportunity to try to develop our…
You did a lot of writing for that band, and arranging. Was that your coming-out party?

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Maynard gave us a lot of opportunity to arrange and to learn about arranging. So we were inspired writing there in that band.

ctx.x: “Mark of Jazz.” Yeah. You were writing hot licks way back then too.

Yeah. Maynard gave us a lot of opportunity to arrange and to learn about arranging. So we were inspired writing there in that band. So there were several guys that were writing a lot. Willie Maiden and Don Sebesky and a couple of other guys that were in the band. Then we were playing arrangements by great arrangers from other bands too.
